questions.question: The <______> tag inserts images into HTML.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <img> is the image tag. Remember: it's not <image> or <picture> - it's the abbreviated <img>.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <img> is the image tag. Remember: it's not <image> or <picture> - it's the abbreviated <img>.

questions.question: The ______ attribute contains the image file path.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: src means source - it's where the browser finds the image file. Can be relative (image.jpg) or absolute (https://...).

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: src means source - it's where the browser finds the image file. Can be relative (image.jpg) or absolute (https://...).

questions.question: ______ text describes images for screen readers.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Alt text (alternative text) describes images for accessibility. It's read by screen readers and shows if images don't load.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Alt text (alternative text) describes images for accessibility. It's read by screen readers and shows if images don't load.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <img> is a self-closing tag (also called void element). It doesn't wrap content, so it closes itself: <img /> or just <img>.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <img> is a self-closing tag (also called void element). It doesn't wrap content, so it closes itself: <img /> or just <img>.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Use alt="" (empty string) for decorative images. Empty alt tells screen readers to skip it, while missing alt causes accessibility issues.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Use alt="" (empty string) for decorative images. Empty alt tells screen readers to skip it, while missing alt causes accessibility issues.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: PNG supports transparency - parts of the image can be completely see-through. JPG doesn't support this feature.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: PNG supports transparency - parts of the image can be completely see-through. JPG doesn't support this feature.

questions.question: width and ______ control image display size.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: width and height attributes control display dimensions. Usually set just one, and the browser calculates the other to maintain aspect ratio.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: width and height attributes control display dimensions. Usually set just one, and the browser calculates the other to maintain aspect ratio.

questions.question: Good alt text helps with ______ (Search Engine Optimization).

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Good alt text improves SEO because search engines can't "see" images - they rely on alt text to understand image content.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Good alt text improves SEO because search engines can't "see" images - they rely on alt text to understand image content.

questions.question: The ______ attribute shows text when hovering over an image.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The title attribute creates a tooltip that appears on hover. It's for additional information, not for accessibility (use alt for that).

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The title attribute creates a tooltip that appears on hover. It's for additional information, not for accessibility (use alt for that).

correct.details: The filename can be any name you choose! folder/image.jpg means "look in the 'folder' subdirectory for 'image.jpg'".

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
